text: Which statement correctly describes positive autoregulation (PAR), in which a transcription factor activates its own gene?
choices: It produces a slower response time than an unregulated gene and, with sufficient cooperativity, can generate bistable, all-or-none switching with memory
It always speeds up the response to steady state by a factor of about two, similar to negative autoregulation
It reduces cell-to-cell variability in protein levels relative to an unregulated gene
It requires a downstream repressor Z to generate a sign-sensitive delay in gene expression
explanation: PAR is slower than an unregulated gene (a 'memory effect') and, when cooperative (Hill coefficient > 1), can create bistability and switch-like, all-or-none expression that persists after the inducing signal is removed. Choices 1 and 2 both describe negative autoregulation, which speeds up responses and reduces noise -- the opposite of PAR. Choice 3 describes a feed-forward loop, which requires three nodes (X, Y, Z), not a single-gene autoregulatory motif.
